links.outcome: LLM numeracy accuracy across semantically equivalent clinical note formats
links.effect: Performance dropped under note-style variation, indicating format sensitivity. Value retrieval was mostly above 85% accuracy; relational comparison and aggregation were weak, with some models below 15%.
links.quote: Fine-tuning on medical data can reduce numeracy relative to base models by over 30%, and performance drops under note-style variation indicate LLM sensitivity to format.

links.outcome: Numeracy of medically fine-tuned LLMs versus their base models
links.effect: Fine-tuning on medical data reduced numeracy relative to base models by over 30%.
links.quote: Fine-tuning on medical data can reduce numeracy relative to base models by over 30%, and performance drops under note-style variation indicate LLM sensitivity to format.

screen.reason: Empirical benchmarking study introducing ClinicNumRobBench to assess the clinical numeracy and robustness of 17 LLMs across different clinical note formats, without evaluating a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
